title: The Funded Completion Lag: Why Growing Enrolments Doesn't Mean Growing Cash for RTOs
linkedin:
A registered training organisation can be growing its enrolments every term and still be quietly running short on cash to deliver them.

That is not a hypothetical. It is the funding structure most government-contracted training providers are working under right now.

Most training contracts pay against completion, not enrolment. A meaningful share of the funding only releases once a unit of competency, a module, or a full qualification is achieved and reported, sometimes months after the student actually enrols.

The delivery cost starts on day one. Trainer wages, resources, assessments and compliance reporting all run from the moment a cohort begins.

The income to cover it can land a full term or more later.

Growth makes this worse, not better. A provider that doubles its intake this term is carrying twice the in-progress delivery cost against a completion pipeline still working through last term's smaller cohort.

The pattern we see across training providers along the East Coast is that the enrolment number keeps everyone optimistic while the completion pipeline is quietly the number that actually predicts the cash position.

The fix isn't slower growth. It's a forecast built around the funding calendar, mapping each cohort to its actual payment trigger, rather than one built around enrolment numbers and an average revenue per student.

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.

Quick question for anyone running a training organisation right now: does your enrolment number and your bank balance ever tell two completely different stories?

It's more common than you'd think. Most training funding pays out when a student completes, not when they enrol, so a growing intake this term can mean a growing gap before the cash catches up.

The businesses that handle it best aren't the ones growing slower. They're the ones who have actually mapped out when each cohort's funding is due to land, instead of just watching the enrolment number climb.

A note for training providers and RTOs across Brisbane, Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria: if your enrolment numbers are climbing this term but your cash position feels tighter than it should, you are not imagining it.

Most government-funded training contracts release a significant share of their funding only once a student completes a unit, a module or the full qualification, and that outcome is often reported through a quarterly funding cycle before payment lands. Meanwhile, the cost of delivery, trainer wages, resources, assessments and compliance reporting, starts from the day the student enrols.

The pattern we see is that growth actually widens this gap rather than closing it. A larger intake this term means more delivery cost sitting ahead of a completion pipeline that is still working through last term's smaller cohort.

The fix is not to slow enrolment growth. It is to forecast cash around the funding calendar itself, mapping each cohort to its actual payment trigger rather than relying on enrolment numbers alone.

If this pattern sounds familiar, it is worth mapping out before the next intake round rather than after the gap has already opened. Read the full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.
